text:
marie: noticing a risky pattern when we flip to private controlplane: full-cluster broadcast for cert/key rotation causes connector fanout and transient overload on endpoint hosts. we should discuss staged rotation + controlplane segmentation. anyone object to a small RFC?

raj: totally agree. blast radius comes from two things: (1) simultaneous TLS handshakes reopening TCP listeners, (2) controlplane broker re-resolving and reconnecting all tenants.

tom: early thoughts for mitigations:
- staged rotation windows (per-region / AZ / tenant-hash buckets) so only ~5-10% reconnect at a time
- connector-side exponential backoff + randomized jitter on handshake failures
- controlplane soft-state: advertise new cert but accept old cert for N minutes to allow overlap
- broker-side dial concurrency limit (configurable token-bucket)

helen: +1. also we should consider splitting controlplane responsibilities: auth & cert mgmt vs routing/relay. If cert management is sharded to a small set of nodes, rotations can be done with fewer edge impacts. that implies a call-path change though.

marie: good point. tradeoffs: sharding reduces fanout but introduces extra hop and survivor set for operator mistakes. staging needs rollout playbook.

raj: sketch of a staggered rotation config (example):
```json
{
  "rotation_policy": "staggered",
  "buckets": 10,
  "bucket_selector": "tenant_id % buckets",
  "bucket_window_seconds": 120
}
```

marie: bucket_window_seconds = 120 means each bucket's connectors will attempt rotation within a two-minute window. combined with connector jitter +/-30s we spread reconnects.

tom: operator playbook additions:
- run canary on bucket 0 (1 tenant) for 1h
- if stable, proceed to buckets 1..3 (10%); wait 30m and check accept-errors and file-descriptor saturation metrics
- pause on FD > 75% or accept-errors > baseline + 5x

helen: metric additions we need: per-endpoint "accept_fd_usage", "connect_retries_per_minute", "tls_bad_cert_rate", and a controlplane gauge for "rotation_in_progress_buckets". Alerting for abnormal concurrent dials.

raj: also consider a quick-bandage: controlplane advertises a grace flag to connectors meaning "defer reconnect for Xs if non-critical". connectors could then pick randomized deferral if they see many peers reconnecting. requires a tiny protocol extension but minimal infra change.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: pushed connector-jitter-2026-04-01 to staging (canary tenant-7). Observability changes pending.

marie: action items:
- raj: draft RFC for staged rotation + controlplane grace flag (include operator playbook + metric thresholds).
- tom: add broker dial limiter and a CLI knob for token-bucket size; quick PR for staging.
- helen: enumerate metrics/alert thresholds and add to dashboards.

helen: timeline: RFC this week, broker PR tomorrow, monitor canary for 48h, then converge on rollout cadence.

marie: thanks all. try to keep the initial RFC tight (design + rollback + test plan). post link here when done.
